flawed_step: Pairwise distinct arc capacities do not imply a unique minimum cut, especially because isolated vertices are permitted.
counterexample: Let V={s,t,a,b}, with the single arc s→t of capacity 1; a and b are isolated. This is a loopless digraph on exactly four vertices, its positive integer arc capacities are pairwise distinct vacuously, and its maximum s-t flow value is 1. The distinct cuts {s} and {s,a} both have capacity 1 (indeed, every s-t cut does), so there is not exactly one minimum cut.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. An isolated vertex can be placed on either side of a cut without changing its capacity, producing distinct minimum cuts.
